# dsh-plugin-openai-quota
**English** · 简体中文 · Changelog · Issues
A one-line quota notice for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It sits at the top edge of the Web UI, stays out
of the way, and never opens a panel:
*A live DSH window (sidebar redacted). The notice runs along the top edge: DeepSeek balance, the cur
rent and weekly ChatGPT quota with their reset times, and the nearest reset-card expiry. The numbers
are whatever your account reports at that moment:*
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Everything comes from accounts you are already signed in to. No API key is created, copied, or store
from accounts you are already signed in to. No API key is created, copied, or stored by this plugin.
## What it shows
| Segment | Source | Notes |

| DeepSeek balance | DSH `deepseekAccount.getBalance()` | CNY wallet, one decimal |
| OpenAI current
quota + reset time | `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` → `rate_limit.primary_window`

| remaining % of the 5-hour window, reset time in `HH:mm` |
| OpenAI weekly quota + weekly reset |

same response → `rate_limit.secondary_window` | remaining % of the weekly window, reset date |
| Res
et cards | `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/rate-limit-reset-credits` | nearest expiry of t
he cards that are still `available` and supported by your plan |
Clicking the reset-card segment opens the ChatGPT usage page in the operating system's default brows
er. The plugin only *tells* you about reset cards — it never redeems one.
## How it works
- **Host half (`index.js`)** reads the existing ChatGPT OAuth grant from DSH's credential store (`ll
m-pi-ai/openai-codex`), calls the two `chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/*` endpoints, reads the DeepSeek

balance through the official `deepseekAccount` service, and serves four authenticated routes.
- **C
lient half (`client.js`)** registers one `shell.overlay` entry (`id: openai-quota`, `order: 600`), f
etches `/openai-quota/summary`, and renders a fixed, click-through, non-interactive status line. It
refreshes every 15 minutes, and immediately when the page becomes visible again.
| Route | Method | Purpose |

| `/openai-quota/summary` | GET | everything the notice renders |
| `/openai-quota/usage` | GET | ra

w quota windows only |
| `/openai-quota/health` | GET | redacted self-check (see Troubleshooting) |
| `/openai-quota/reset-card/open` | POST | opens the usage page in the default browser |
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the Web UI (desktop app or `dsh web`).
- A ChatGPT/Codex sign-in already con

figured in DSH — this is what supplies the OpenAI quota.
- Optional: a signed-in DeepSeek account fo
r the balance segment. Without it the balance renders as `—`.

## Configuration
None. The refresh interval, timezone (`Asia/Shanghai`), and target URLs are constants so the plugin
cannot be pointed at another host or turned into an open redirect. Fork the repo if you want differe
pointed at another host or turned into an open redirect. Fork the repo if you want different values.
## Security and privacy
- **No admin key, ever.** The plugin reuses the OAuth grant DSH already holds; it never asks for an

`sk-…` key.
- **Credentials stay Host-side.** The browser only ever sees percentages, timestamps, an

d card counts — the access token never leaves the Host process.
- **Every route sits behind the loca
l trust check** (`connection.requestRejection`) and fails closed: no connection service → `503 local

-auth-unavailable`, rejected call → `401/403`, guard throws → `403 local-auth-failed`.
- **Method al

lowlists per route**, so a browser `GET` cannot trigger the opener (`405 method-not-allowed`).
- **N
o request input reaches the browser command.** The URL is a Host constant and is passed as its own `

spawn` argument; nothing from the request is interpolated into a shell.
- **Minimal upstream payload
.** Account email, plan type, and credit details are dropped on the Host before anything is returned
** Account email, plan type, and credit details are dropped on the Host before anything is returned.
## Known limits
- The `chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/*` endpoints are internal to the ChatGPT web app. They can chang

e or disappear at any time; the notice degrades to `—` / `暂不可用` instead of breaking the UI.
- In the
**desktop app** the shell hands `window.open` to the default browser and returns no window handle,
so the usage page opens at the top — the notice cannot scroll it to the reset-card section. When the
GUI runs in a real browser tab, the plugin re-navigates that tab with a text-fragment directive and

*does* land on the reset-card section.
- Reset times are always rendered in `Asia/Shanghai`, not th

e local timezone of the machine.
- The quota windows are reported as ChatGPT labels them (`primary_w
indow` = 5-hour, `secondary_window` = weekly). If your plan exposes different windows, the labels si
mply follow the data.
## Troubleshooting
`GET /openai-quota/health` returns a redacted snapshot:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Symptom | Meaning |
| `credentialConfigured: false` | No ChatGPT sign-in found for `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex`; sign in to

ChatGPT in DSH first |
| `usageError: "upstream-http"` + `upstreamStatus: 401` | The OAuth grant exp

ired — sign in again |
| `usageError: "upstream-unreachable"` | Network/proxy blocked `chatgpt.com`

|
| `windows.primary_window: false` | The upstream response changed shape; the notice shows `—` |
|

Notice shows `读取失败` | The summary route failed or the browser lost the local auth cookie |
| Clickin
g the reset card does nothing | The notice sits inside the desktop window's drag strip; the link alr
eady sets `-webkit-app-region: no-drag`, so report an issue with your DSH version |
